measurement_basis: authenticated Environment campaign activity, Control source inspection, and a bounded regression reproduction

observation.source_interface: MNCS Control Environment RPC claim recovery

request.failure_mode: The same-operator recovery parser forwarded the requested worktree and branch but dropped --paths. Recovery then evaluated the broad worktree scope, so multiple otherwise-disjoint claims could make a legitimate narrow recovery ambiguous.
request.reproduction_basis: Control regression test constructs disjoint and overlapping live claims and verifies that an explicit narrow path request selects only the overlapping claim while a broad request remains fail-closed.

outcome.interpretation: A concrete claim-recovery scope defect was present in the Control bridge. This is evidence of one authorization-path limitation; it does not establish the cause of every prior pickup, merge, or publish difficulty.

related_work.work_intent_goal: exercise canonical Environment persistence through the Control socket
related_work.campaign_objective: MNCS Environmental Capability Intelligence and Continuous Improvement, including capability accountability and machine-native adoption

pressure_hypothesis.title: Same-operator claim recovery loses requested path scope
pressure_hypothesis.subsystem: MNCS Control Environment RPC and Environment claim recovery
pressure_hypothesis.actionable_recommendation: Preserve the exact requested path set when deriving same-operator recovery candidates; refuse malformed or empty path scopes rather than widening them, while retaining host-liveness and conservative overlap checks.
not_measured: whether this defect caused any specific earlier campaign delay
frequency of ambiguous same-operator recovery requests in production
behavior during sustained concurrent use after deployment
a live stale-claim recovery before the fix
whether this was the sole cause of the user's repeated pickup and delivery difficulties
